rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report a two-year (2018-2019) pot experiment in a greenhouse at Jiangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences with four treatments (CK, LM, MM, HM micro-nano bubble water), 30 pots per treatment, measuring yield, tillers, SPAD, Pn, roots, biomass and N uptake (Tables 1-3, Figures 1-3).
rows.notes: The study is a primary pot experiment on micro-nano bubble (oxygenated) irrigation water applied to flooded potted double-cropping rice; water was added every 5 days from a graduated container, not by drip irrigation. The claim row is classified under drip technology. The yield figure in the passage (up to 14.31%) matches the study's own result for HM late rice in 2018 (Table 1; Section 3.1: LM/MM/HM late rice +6.10/12.81/14.31% over CK in 2018, early rice +5.43/7.77/10.95%), with means <U+00B1> SD reported and DO in soil solution measured (Figure 1) as the intermediate variable, and the authors note limitations (ideal greenhouse pot conditions, no rain, limited MNB concentration from the air-source pump, field extension untested). However, because the irrigation technology is MNB-water flood irrigation in pots rather than drip, Q2 is answered no with technology_mismatch; if the reviewer's technology were read as MNB irrigation generally, Q2, Q4, Q8 and Q9 would be yes and Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7 no (single site, pots only, one measurement method for yield, no stated requirement conditions).

notes: Text is complete though the Methods section (pp. 2-3) is garbled by overlapping page layout; content was recoverable. Study is a greenhouse pot experiment with MNB-oxygenated water, not a drip irrigation trial.
